# GoHighLevel API Key: How to Get API Access in 2026

The old API key is retired. Here is how I get API access now, with Private Integration tokens, OAuth apps, the right headers and the rate limits.

When I first connected GoHighLevel to other tools, I copied an API key from the settings and pasted it in. That's still what most tutorials tell you to do, but it's out of date. HighLevel retired API v1, and new v1 keys can't be created anymore. In this guide I show you what replaced the API key, how I create a Private Integration token, how to make your first API v2 request, and the rate limits and webhook details I wish I'd known earlier. Everything here is checked against HighLevel's help center and developer docs, with screens from my own account.

#### Short version

- **API v1 reached end of support on 31 December 2025**, and new v1 keys can't be created.
- Use a **Private Integration token** from Settings, then Private Integrations.
- **API access is on every plan**, including Starter.
- Every request needs a **Bearer token and a Version header**.

## The short answer

To get API access in GoHighLevel today, create a Private Integration token. In your sub-account or agency, go to Settings, then Private Integrations, click Create new Integration, give it a name, pick only the scopes you need, and copy the token. HighLevel shows it only once, so store it somewhere safe.

Then send it with every request to `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com` as `Authorization: Bearer` plus a `Version` header. If you don't have an account yet, HighLevel's standard trial is 14 days, but my link gives you 30 days free, which is plenty of time to build and test an integration.

## What happened to the GoHighLevel API key

The old API key was the v1 way of connecting to HighLevel. It gave unrestricted access to the v1 API. Private Integration tokens replace it with scoped access to API v2, so each token can only do what you allow.

### API v1 end of support

HighLevel's API documentation article says "V1 APIs has reached end-of-support as on 31-December-2025." Existing integrations keep working, but they get no support or updates. All current docs live at `marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs`.

![HighLevel API Documentation landing page with the Get Started with API button highlighted](https://upmish.com/wp-content/themes/upmish/assets/articles/gohighlevel-api-key/gohighlevel-api-key-05-dev-docs.webp)

### Legacy keys that expire after 90 days

According to HighLevel's API security article, inactive legacy keys, both agency and location keys, are marked Expired after 90 days without use. Expired keys stay visible in settings and can be rotated or refreshed, but new v1 key creation is no longer supported. My agency settings menu still shows an API Keys item next to Private Integrations, but for anything new I use a Private Integration.

## Which plans include API access

This is a common question, and the answer is better than many people expect. HighLevel says API access is on all plans.

| Plan | Price | API access |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | $97/mo | OAuth 2.0, Private Integration tokens and standard endpoints |
| Unlimited | $297/mo | OAuth 2.0, Private Integration tokens and standard endpoints |
| Agency Pro | $497/mo | Everything above, plus Agency Pro-restricted endpoints |

HighLevel doesn't list which endpoints are Agency Pro-restricted in that article, so check the endpoint reference before you build on one. You can compare everything else in each plan on the [GoHighLevel pricing page](https://www.gohighlevel.com/pricing?fp_ref=upmish), and my [GoHighLevel pricing guide](https://upmish.com/gohighlevel-pricing/) explains the differences.

## Private Integration token vs OAuth app

HighLevel gives you two ways to authenticate with API v2. Here's how they compare, from the API documentation article and the Private Integrations docs:

| | Private Integration token | OAuth app |
|---|---|---|
| Who it's for | Internal tools and single accounts | Public or Marketplace apps |
| How the token is made | Created in Settings, shown once | User installs and approves the app |
| Refresh | Static until you rotate it | Access tokens expire daily |
| Scopes | Picked when you create it, editable later | Set on the app |
| Best use | Zapier, Make, n8n or your own script | Multi-location access with user approval |

For most agencies and business owners, a Private Integration is the right choice. I only reach for OAuth when I'm building an app other accounts will install.

## How to create a Private Integration token

You can create up to 20 Private Integrations at agency level and 20 at sub-account level. Here's how I do it:

1. Go to Settings, then Private Integrations, in the sub-account or in your agency settings.
2. Click Create new Integration.
3. Enter a name and a description, so your team knows what the token is for.
4. Pick only the scopes the tool needs.
5. Create the integration and copy the token. HighLevel shows it only once.
6. Store it in a password manager or a secrets store, never in a shared doc.
7. Use one token per tool, such as one for Zapier, one for Make and one for n8n.

![GoHighLevel sub-account Settings, Private Integrations list with the Create New Integration button highlighted](https://upmish.com/wp-content/themes/upmish/assets/articles/gohighlevel-api-key/gohighlevel-api-key-02-subaccount-private-integrations.webp)

![GoHighLevel Create new Integration screen with the Basic info step showing Name and Description fields](https://upmish.com/wp-content/themes/upmish/assets/articles/gohighlevel-api-key/gohighlevel-api-key-03-create-scopes.webp)

The agency version looks the same, and lives in your agency Settings menu.

![GoHighLevel agency Settings, Private Integrations empty state with the Create new integration button highlighted](https://upmish.com/wp-content/themes/upmish/assets/articles/gohighlevel-api-key/gohighlevel-api-key-04-agency-private-integrations.webp)

### Editing scopes later

If a tool needs more access later, you don't have to make a new token. HighLevel lets you edit the name and scopes of a Private Integration without changing the token, so nothing breaks in the tools that already use it.

### Rotating a token

HighLevel recommends rotating Private Integration tokens every 90 days. When you rotate one, the old and new tokens both work for 7 days, so you have time to update every tool before the old one stops working.

## Your first API v2 request

Every API v2 request goes to the same base URL and needs two headers: your token as a Bearer token, and a Version header. Here's a minimal request that reads one location. Replace the placeholders with your own location ID and token:

```
curl -X GET "https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/locations/YOUR_LOCATION_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_PRIVATE_INTEGRATION_TOKEN" \
  -H "Version: 2021-07-28" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
```

A few notes on the Version header. HighLevel's docs list v3 as the latest version, plus 2023-02-21, 2021-07-28 and 2021-04-15, and say the three dated versions expose the same endpoints. Whichever version's docs you build from, send that Version value and don't mix versions in one integration. Also check the required scope for each endpoint in the reference, and give your token that scope before you call it.

If you'd rather not write code at all, my [GoHighLevel Zapier guide](https://upmish.com/gohighlevel-zapier-integration/) and [GoHighLevel vs n8n comparison](https://upmish.com/gohighlevel-vs-n8n/) show the no-code routes.

## Rate limits and the headers to watch

For Marketplace apps using OAuth, HighLevel's default limits are counted per app per resource, where a resource is one location or company:

1. **Burst:** 100 API requests per 10 seconds.
2. **Daily:** 200,000 API requests per day.

Each install gets its own budget, so installing an app on more sub-accounts doesn't split your allowance. HighLevel's rate limits page also has a section on Private Integration tokens and says they're counted differently, so read it before you plan a heavy Private Integration job.

![HighLevel developer docs Rate Limits page with the burst and daily limits table highlighted](https://upmish.com/wp-content/themes/upmish/assets/articles/gohighlevel-api-key/gohighlevel-api-key-06-rate-limits.webp)

Your responses tell you where you stand. These are the headers HighLevel lists:

1. `X-RateLimit-Limit-Daily` and `X-RateLimit-Daily-Remaining` for the daily limit.
2. `X-RateLimit-Max` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining` for the burst limit.
3. `X-RateLimit-Interval-Milliseconds` for the length of the burst window.

## Building a Marketplace app with OAuth 2.0

If you're building an app that other agencies or sub-accounts will install, you use OAuth 2.0. From HighLevel's OAuth docs, the steps are:

1. Create the app in the Marketplace dashboard.
2. Set the scopes your app needs under Advanced Settings, then Auth.
3. Add your redirect URL.
4. When someone installs the app, your server exchanges the code for access and refresh tokens.
5. Refresh the access token before it expires, because OAuth access tokens expire daily.

If you plan to resell HighLevel to clients under your own brand, my [GoHighLevel SaaS Mode guide](https://upmish.com/gohighlevel-saas-mode/) covers that side.

## Webhooks

Marketplace apps can receive webhook events. In your app, go to Advanced Settings, then Webhooks, enter your URL and turn on the events you want. The App Install event is subscribed by default. Events cover contacts, opportunities, tasks, appointments, invoices and more.

Verify every webhook before you trust it. HighLevel's current signature header is `X-GHL-Signature`, which uses Ed25519. The legacy `X-WH-Signature` header, which uses RSA, was scheduled for deprecation on 1 September 2026, so make sure your code checks `X-GHL-Signature`.

If you only need webhooks inside your own account, look at workflows first. My [GoHighLevel workflow templates](https://upmish.com/gohighlevel-workflow-templates/) are a good place to start.

## Security habits I follow

1. **Pick the fewest scopes.** A token that only reads contacts can't delete anything.
2. **Use one token per tool.** If one leaks, I revoke one token, not all of them.
3. **Rotate on a schedule.** Every 90 days, using the 7-day overlap to update my tools.
4. **Never share tokens in public.** No screenshots, public code or support chats with a token in them. I blurred everything in the screens above.

The same thinking applies to AI tools. My guide to [connecting GoHighLevel to Claude](https://upmish.com/connect-gohighlevel-to-claude/) shows how I give an assistant access safely.

## Common questions

Where do I find my GoHighLevel API key?

For new integrations you create a Private Integration token instead. Go to Settings, then Private Integrations, in your sub-account or agency, and click Create new Integration. HighLevel no longer supports creating new v1 API keys.

Does GoHighLevel still support API v1?

No. HighLevel says API v1 reached end of support on 31 December 2025. Existing v1 integrations keep working, but they get no support or updates, so I'd move them to API v2.

Is the GoHighLevel API available on the Starter plan?

Yes. HighLevel says API access is on all plans, including Starter at $97 a month. OAuth 2.0, Private Integration tokens and the standard endpoints work on every plan. Only some endpoints are restricted to Agency Pro.

What is a Private Integration token?

It's a static OAuth2 access token that gives scoped access to API v2 for one agency or sub-account. You choose the scopes when you create it, and HighLevel shows the token only once.

Should I use a Private Integration or OAuth?

Use a Private Integration for an internal tool or a single account. Use OAuth for a public or Marketplace app, access across many locations, or when users need to approve access themselves.

What are the GoHighLevel API rate limits?

For Marketplace apps using OAuth, the default limits are 100 requests per 10 seconds and 200,000 requests per day, per app per location or company. Each install gets its own budget.

What Version header should I send?

Every API v2 request needs a Version header. HighLevel's docs list v3 as the latest, plus 2023-02-21, 2021-07-28 and 2021-04-15. Send the value that matches the docs you build from, and don't mix versions.

Do Private Integration tokens expire?

No, they stay the same until you rotate them. HighLevel recommends rotating them every 90 days, and when you do, the old and new tokens both work for 7 days so you can update your tools.

### The verdict

The GoHighLevel API key you see in old tutorials is gone for new work. Private Integration tokens replaced it, and they're better: scoped, rotatable and available on every plan. Once you have a token and send the right headers, API v2 is easy to work with.

1. **Use a Private Integration** for your own tools and single accounts.
2. **Use OAuth** when you build an app other accounts will install.
3. **Send a Version header** on every request, and watch the rate limit headers.

New to HighLevel? My [tutorial for beginners](https://upmish.com/gohighlevel-tutorial-for-beginners/) and [30 day free trial guide](https://upmish.com/gohighlevel-30-day-free-trial/) are good next reads, and [what LeadConnector is](https://upmish.com/what-is-leadconnector/) explains why the API lives on a leadconnectorhq.com address.

Details come from HighLevel's help center articles on the API, Private Integrations, API security and migration, and its developer docs on authorization, versions, rate limits, OAuth and webhooks, read 4 Nov 2026, plus screens from our own GoHighLevel account. HighLevel updates its API docs often, so check them before you build.
